value.project_name: Food safety systems and trade facilitation across agri-food value chains in Somalia
value.description: The proposed project is part of an EU-INTPA regional programme called ¿Alliance for the Horn of Africa Initiative¿. In this framework, UNIDO has been offered the opportunity to design a project proposal set to strengthening Somalia overall capacities of quality control and standards institutions for inspections, metrology, testing, and certification of priority food products (through standards development, laboratories, equipment, staff training, etc.), including certification of origin, as well as improve collaboration among quality control, standards and certification institutions and with relevant Somali public institutions (e.g. customs, port/airport authorities, police, statistics, Ministries of Commerce and Industry, Agriculture and Fisheries) and private sector. The collaboration set to be put forward by the proposed project, will also include outreach, engagements and partnership facilitation with international standards bodies and institutions from other countries in particular Kenya, Ethiopia and UAE. This will have the very specific objective to move towards the overall international recognition of Somali standards, certification system and its alignment with international best practices. Ultimately, this will in turn, help increase the international recognition of Somali products, starting from selected food products that the proposed project will be directly supporting as part of this intervention.

value.project_name: Les jeunes comme acteurs de changement dans la lutte contre les violences basées sur le genre
value.description: Contract related to: Les jeunes comme acteurs de changement dans la lutte contre les violences basées sur le genre - Human rights and democracy are founding values of the EU. Protecting and promoting HR&D is therefore a key priority of the EU¿s external action. It is also a precondition for sustainable development and for building more inclusive, open and resilient societies.Yet, recent data show that globally, most countries are far from having acceptable human rights and democracy track records. In this context, worsened by the COVID crisis, the EU re-affirmed its commitment to support human rights and democracy worldwide by adopting the `Action Plan on Human Rights and Democracy 2020-2024¿. The Action Plan identifies priorities and key actions, to ensure that the EU plays a greater role in promoting and defending human rights and democracy throughout its external action. The Regulation (EU) 2021/947 (Global Europe) establishes the legal basis for the human rights and democracy actions. Particularly, its annex III details the areas of intervention for human rights and democracy.The overall objective of the present action is to contribute to promote and protect human rights and fundamental freedoms, democracy and the rule of law worldwide. The action will achieve this objective by supporting and strengthening civil society organisations (CSOs), democracy activists and human-rights defenders working on critical human rights and democracy issues in non-EU countries. It may also cover, where relevant, the promotion of international humanitarian law. Consequently, it will contribute to the 5 priorities of the Multiannual Indicative programme 2021-2027 as well as the specific priorities set out for the additional funding coming from the cushion.This action will mainly be implemented by EU Delegations in-country so as to: (i) better respond to the country-specific contexts; (ii) be as close as possible to the needs of the rights holders; and (iii) promote a sense of `ownership¿ of the action among local actors. The actions financed at country level will be in line with: (i) the EU action plan for human rights and democracy; (ii) EU guidelines on human rights; and (iii) the respective Human Rights and Democracy country strategies or priorities under the EU accession process. All actions will follow a human rights based approach putting people at the centre of actions and also focusing on promoting gender equality.

value.project_name: Promoting Ethiopian trade and economic integration through private-led value chains development
value.description:
Support the active engagement of the private sector in AfCFTA¿s successful implementation in Ethiopia, including labour mobility and the movement of business people.

Activities relating to Output 1.4:

- Enhance human and institutional capacity of private firms to access the AfCFTA Market through knowledge and skills trainings ¿ including on climate resilience, and on the movement of business people;

- Build the capacity of the Ethiopian Chamber of Commerce and Sectoral Association (ECCSA) through the provision of advisory services, the creation of a Private-Public Dialogue Forum, and/or technical support;

- Support sector-specific associations through studies, trainings, drafting of export guides, and support to participation to trade events;

- Increase efficiency in supply chains through studies and decreasing non-tariff barriers;

- Strengthen trade promotion activities related to AfCFTA markets through studies, development on an online platform to connect Ethiopian and African businesses, improve access to credit and fund participation to trade fairs;

- Provide trainings to the Ethiopian Ministry of Trade and Regional Integration (MoTRI);

- Support academic, research, and other institutions to design and deliver trainings and/or a Master programme on trade, and to provide demand-driven research, including on the movement of business people;

- Establish a think tank group with trade experts and other relevant stakeholders ¿ including security experts.

value.project_name: Ground water development for climate resilience in low land pastoral areas of Ethiopia bordering Somalia and Kenya
value.description:
The proposed action aims to contribute to increased access to permanent water supply for the drought-affected population in the eastern and southern pastoral and agro-pastoral areas of Ethiopia through development of safely managed and sustainable ground water exploitations. The action location focus along the border of Ethiopia with Somalia and Kenya

Indicative activities are:

  1. Ground water mapping to identify ground water abstraction suitable locations in the eastern and southern pastoral and agro-pastoral areas bordering Somali and Kenya. This include: water points inventory and water quality survey, updating geological maps, ground water suitability maps, hydrogeological conceptual models and operational maps (geophysical survey, geochemistry analysis, remote sensing (RS) data and analysis).
  2. Drilling of up to 30 boreholes, installation of solar pumping systems and construction of all the needed infrastructures including reservoirs and distribution points at strategic locations along the border to Somalia and Kenya.
  3. Strengthen the capacity of the regional and local governments in improving groundwater feasibility studies and cloud-based ground water data management systems.
